description.narrative: Under-investment remains a huge constraint for biodiversity conservation: the financing gap for the Philippine Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (PBSAP 2024-2040) is USD 1.24 billion/year . In response, the DENR BMB and UNDP initiated Phase II of the BIOFIN Project to build capacity and support various finance solutions. The following barriers remain to fully implement the National Biodiversity Finance Plan (NBFP): weak institutional capacities for resource mobilization; low public/private sector investments for biodiversity; biodiversity investments not benefiting IPLCs; increasing agricultural subsidies impacting biodiversity; and limited participation of local governments and private sector in biodiversity investments. The project aims to increase public and private sector biodiversity investments and reduce financial flows with incidental environmental impacts to support the KMGBF-aligned PBSAP targets. Four components will deliver the project outcomes: (1) Improved management effectiveness of NBFP implementation, (2) Increased financing for local BSAPs, (3) Reduced agriculture-related subsidies with incidental environmental impacts, and (4) Effective Advocacy and Partnerships. By supporting financing of the PBSAP, these outcomes will directly benefit 7,000 people especially IPLCs, and improved management of 70,833 ha of terrestrial protected areas (PAs), 46,985 ha of Marine PAs, 19,900 ha of restored land and ecosystems, 29,000 ha of landscapes and 32,000 ha of marine habitats under improved practices. The project aims to generate increased biodiversity finance equivalent to 30% of the financing gap, i.e. USD 372,413,793. Subsidies with negative environmental impacts will be reduced by 25% in the targeted landscapes.

condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

The Implementing Partner shall ensure that all of its obligations set forth under the section entitled “Legal Context and/or Risk Management Standard Clauses” are passed on to each responsible party, subcontractor and sub-recipient and that all the clauses under this section entitled “Risk Management” are included, mutatis mutandis, in all sub-contracts or sub-agreements entered into further to the Project Document
